comments.text:
As someone who still have to fight this type of darkness, I can say honestly, it is just like William Afton. 
It always comes back. 

Sometimes you succeed, other times you fail. But what makes this darkness so hard to defeat, compared to some other negative experiences that you just abandon when you remember the good ones, is that  this one kind of tricks you to feel that you live inside a good experience, when in reality the only thing you do is to leave your own life to lose value and waste. 

When you succeed just feels so good,
But When you fail, it reloads back to the full power it had over you from the start. 

It will need a lot of time to pass for that toxic bond to trully get weaker and weaker. The more you resist without it, the less influence it does have over you. So from a giant wall of darkness, it can become in time just like that annoying mosquito who buzzzes but never gets a chance to trully bite. 


So, for every single one person that struggle in this battle, find reasons to spend time outside of this void. Quality time. The more you do, the less will have effect against you, even when it returns. Cause it does. 
I was just like you brothers and sisters. There is no better victory than leaving this behind. 

William Afton may always come back, but will be soon enough just a painful memory from the past, not worth remembering anymore. 

Come closer to GOD and to the light HE offers. And you will see how the darkness dissapears. 

Amen to every single one of you, noble warriors. God Bless you in this journey.

comments.text:
I think I was 13 or 14 when it all started. I don't remember exactly. But I do remember where it began. In the boys' bathroom at school.
A friend showed me a video. It wasn't even that bad, but back then I was a pretty innocent kid. Small things could shock me, and that video stuck with me.
I didn't think much of it after that. But at school, all the boys talked about was girls, snaps, and dirty stuff. Eventually, I got curious too.
I still remember the first time I searched for it alone. I just sat there, staring at the screen, not really knowing what I was watching. I can even remember parts of that exact video. I felt a strange urge to pee, so I went to the bathroom. Nothing. I came back, then went again. This happened a few times until I started touching myself. And that's how it began.
Eight years later, I'm still struggling.
My parents never deserved this. And somehow, God has kept it hidden all these years. Sometimes I think He knows I can beat this on my own. But other times, I feel like I'll be stuck with it forever.
I've tried so many times to stop. Yet here I am. Sometimes I even wonder if I deserve anything good.
I try to picture myself at 60, with grandkids, looking back at who I am today. Hoping that one day, all of this will feel small and far away.
But right now, it's hard.
